title: Prefetch & Batching Cost Playbook — CedarWorks (Optimize Walkthrough)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations for CedarWorks: prefix/KV prefetch options, batching strategies, and a cost-sensitivity model. Agreed to run a sandbox sim with CedarWorks production trace and to share SOC2 + KMS whitepaper.
topics: deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-07-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Lena (CedarWorks Head of ML), Arman (Platform), Sophie (CTO)
Shared artifacts: cedar-sim-worksheet (https://redwood.app/sim/cedarworks), SOC2 and KMS whitepaper (link shared in chat)

Summary (auto): Went through Optimize console recommendations for reducing per-token costs via KV prefix prefetch and dynamic batching. Ran a quick cost-sensitivity scenario on a 1M monthly active users (MAU) conversational assistant. Action: Redwood to run sandbox with Cedar trace; Cedar to confirm latency SLO and provide sample traffic.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hi everyone uh welcome, thanks for making time. we've got about 50 minutes, we'll run through the optimize playbook, show the console scenarios and then leave time for q&a.
00:17 Speaker 2 (Jonah): hey, quick intro from me — i'm Jonah, i'm going to jump into the econ sim and show the prefetch model and how TTL and batch size move the needle.
00:27 Lena: thanks. quick context — cedarworks runs a mixed voice+text assistant, avg input length is small but we have a heavy tail, and p95 latency budget is 450ms.
00:40 Sophie: we're evaluating both hosted and private; main thing is cost predictability and data residency for EMEA.
00:49 Maya: perfect, we'll keep that in mind — i'll call out hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs.

02:03 Jonah: ok first slide, high level. two big levers: batching (collecting concurrent requests) and caching — specifically prefix/KV cache for sessionized conversations, and lookahead prefetch for expected continuations.
02:22 Jonah: the console recommends a prefetch window based on session heatmap, we can autoconfigure a TTL. for cedar's profile i'd start with a 30s TTL for active sessions and a 10k prefix size cap.
02:34 Arman: 30s seems short — how does that interact with concurrency? if we have lots of concurrent small sessions, will we waste gpu cycles?
02:44 Jonah: great Q. the model in the sim assumes prefetch runs opportunistically only when the session is active and there is a predicted next-token probability above threshold. we also show a batched prefetch path that groups prefetches with normal regen batches to amortize cost.

05:10 Speaker 3 (Lena): can you show an example cost calc? like with our numbers, what savings do we expect?
05:18 Jonah: yes — loaded the cedar trace into the sim. baseline: no cache, conservative batch size 1 (low latency) -> ~ $12k/mo for inference tokens. With prefix prefetch + batch size 4 amortization, and 35% cache hit rate from the trace, we simulated $6.8k/mo, roughly 43% savings.
05:45 Sophie: that seems optimistic — what's the sensitivity if hit rate is lower?
05:51 Jonah: i toggled hit rate: at 20% hits savings drop to ~25%; at 50% it's closer to 55%. TTL, prefix size, and prediction threshold are the main knobs.
06:10 Maya: also note tradeoffs: prefetch increases short-term p50 but can reduce p95 if hits occur — need to respect your 450ms p95 SLO.

08:30 Arman: about deployment — if we go VPC/private, how does prefetch touch our data? encryption?
08:39 Maya: prefetch runs in the same runtime as inference. for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) you keep data in your network; keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM. logs can be routed to your SIEM, and we support end-to-end TLS.
08:58 Lena: do you have SOC2 + KMS docs?
09:02 Maya: yes — shared in chat, and we'll attach to the follow-up.

11:12 Jonah: jumping back to batching, the console sim shows two batching regimes: latency-first (batch size 1-2, low batching window) and throughput-first (batch size 8-16, higher batching window). we recommend dynamic batching where latency SLOs trigger fallbacks.
11:38 Jonah: dynamic batching is runtime-based: if queueing time would breach your p95, we reduce batch window to avoid added tail latency. otherwise we target a target-batch size to optimize cost.

13:05 Lena: how do you measure queue add latency? is it per-region?
13:10 Jonah: yes per-route and per-region. console exposes histograms; you can set per-route SLOs.

15:40 Speaker 2 (Jonah): small demo — opened the optimize console, loaded cedar sim. here's the slider for TTL, here's batch window, and the right-hand panel shows cost delta and p95 transform.
15:58 Jonah: note the console shows estimated token savings and per-1000-user cost — it's a Monte Carlo sim under the hood that samples from your trace.
16:20 Lena: oh i see — the sim also flags risk cases, e.g., cold-starts, model switch events, and long-running sessions.

18:00 Arman: on evictions — if prefix cache evicts aggressively, do we get metrics to tune eviction policy?
18:07 Jonah: yes — hit/loss callbacks, eviction counters, and a session heatmap. we recommend TTL+LRU with a size cap per runtime.

20:25 Sophie: any implications for concurrency and reserved capacity (Dedicated)? we want predictable throughput for peak sales cycles.
20:33 Maya: Dedicated gives you committed GPUs and predictable throughput. caching and prefetch reduce the GPU token load so you can right-size the dedicated pool. we can model committed vs burst cost in the sim.

23:50 Speaker 4 (Lena): ok can we talk about fallback behavior — if prefetch fails or model variant unavailable?
23:58 Jonah: in the routing layer we have a fallback policy: if a prefetch miss or runtime OOM occurs the request falls back to a cold path on compatible model variant or to a lower-cost region based on your policy. console shows projected SLA hit probability for each fallback.
24:25 Arman: is there a way to force bypass for very sensitive requests?
24:29 Maya: yes, per-route tags allow bypassing prefetch/batch, and you can mark routes as high-priority to get dedicated concurrency lanes.

27:40 Jonah: small gotcha — tokenization differences across models can change cost math. we included a tokenization correction factor in the sim; it's adjustable per model.

29:15 Lena: are there any vendor lock-in concerns with prefetch logic? like if we wanted to move off Redwood?
29:24 Maya: the prefetch approach uses standard model APIs; we export a config and a lightweight client you can run. moving is doable but you'll need to port your cache population logic.

31:00 Sophie: security double-check — does prefetch ever persist PII in cache? how do you handle redaction?
31:08 Jonah: by default we treat caches as ephemeral and encrypted; for PII we recommend token-level masking before prefetch and we support an allow-list/deny-list on route config. for Private deployments you can enable HSM-backed KMS and set retention policies.

33:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick live tweak — i changed TTL to 60s and batch target to 6 in the sim; results show marginally higher hit rate but p95 creeps up by ~40ms.
33:40 Lena: 40ms is okay for us if it buys 20% more savings.
33:44 Arman: what about model quantization? does that change the calculus?
33:49 Jonah: yes. quantization reduces per-token GPU cost, so even with same hit rates the absolute $ savings are different. we let you set the model cost profile in the sim (float16 vs 4-bit quant).

36:10 Speaker 2 (Jonah): we also demoed a scenario that uses a small on-device reranker to improve prefetch accuracy — that lowers false-prefetch and improves hit rate but adds a tiny CPU cost.
36:33 Lena: interesting, we'd consider that for high-frequency routes.

38:05 Sophie: how soon can we run a sandbox with our trace? we want the exact numbers before we commit to dedicated.
38:12 Maya: we can spin up a sandbox in the next 3 business days if Cedar provides a sampled trace and the p95 SLO. we need a CSV with timestamp, route, input length, and session id, roughly 100k rows min.
38:30 Arman: we can export that. i'll follow up.

40:01 Speaker 5 (Jonah): quick note about costs: the sim shows both variable (per-token inference) and fixed (reserved GPUs) lines. sometimes prefetch reduces variable enough that fixed reserved capacity becomes the dominant cost — that's when we recommend autoscaling or hybrid reserved+burst.

42:15 Lena: any competitor features to watch out for?
42:20 Maya: some competitors offer simpler session caches but lack dynamic batching + routing fallbacks; others have proprietary prefetch heuristics but no end-to-end cost sim.
42:34 (low audio) Speaker 6: [inaudible]

44:00 Sophie: ok let's recap next steps and owners.

45:12 Maya: recap — Redwood will: 1) run the sandbox sim with Cedar trace; 2) send SOC2/KMS docs; 3) share the console workbook and the monte-carlo assumptions; 4) propose dates for an infra deep-dive with SEs.
45:29 Lena: Cedar will: 1) provide sampled trace and p95 SLO; 2) confirm target routes for pilot; 3) review initial cost sheet.
45:40 Maya: timing? can we get the trace by next Tue?
45:45 Arman: yes we can have a trace by 2028-07-17.
45:49 Maya: great. we'll aim to have the sandbox sim results back by 2028-07-20.

52:00 Jonah: any final q's?
52:07 Lena: none from me, thanks this was helpful.
52:12 Sophie: no — thanks all.
